label: <DEL> step (esp. first token x/l, short seqs) + early first e input
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) Delimiter step (76% of activation mass): fires on 7% of <DEL> steps, most often and most strongly when the sequence is short (L=3-4) and when the first original token (the token about to be recalled) is x or l. The top activations are all <DEL> in sequences starting with x or l, e.g. x p v s <DEL>. (2) Input e during the original phase (23% of mass, weaker): fires on the first occurrence of e, mainly early (t<=3). At t=0 it is perfectly precise, but magnitude there is small. Almost never fires in the copy phase (0.8% of mass) or on any input token other than e or <DEL>. The <DEL> part depends on graded sequence content that a simple predicate cannot capture, so precision stays limited (dev F1 0.51; covering all <DEL> steps with L<=5 raises mass recall to 0.84 but lowers precision to 0.23).
